newsitem.title: USA: U.S stocks end higher as techs, bonds bounce.
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks end higher as techs, bonds bounce.

text.p: U.S. stocks moved higher, led by a rebound in technology shares and aided by a bond market rally after three days of losses.

"We're still in the doldrums, but at least we had a little more life today. We did have a decent bond market despite a lackluster two-year note auction and strong consumer confidence numbers," said Larry Wachtel, a market analyst at Prudential Securities. "But we're still in a vacuum -- there are no serious players in stocks or bonds this week."
The Dow industrials rose 17 to about 5711.
PepsiCo was the most active NYSE issue, off 1/2 to 31 on about 7.6 million shares. Salomon Brothers executed an unusually huge three million-share block trade.
Olympic Financial rose 2-1/2 to 26-3/8 on continued takeover speculation. The shares jumped 6-1/4 Monday after news that a possible acquirer had indicated interest in buying Olympic Financial.
British Petroleum lost 7/8 to 118-1/8 in U.S. trading. Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock to neutral from outperform on a price basis.

WorldCom fell 1-3/4 to 21 after losing 3-5/8 Monday on news of its multi-billion dollar merger pact with MFS Communications. MFS, which climbed 9-15/16 Monday, fell 3-8/16 to 41-5/16. Merrill cut MFS and First Boston raised WorldCom.

Consolidated Freightways rose 1-3/4 to 23-5/8 after news it plans to spin off its long-haul, less-than-truckload units. Morgan Stanley upgraded the stock to outperform from neutral. Consolidated Freightway's gains helped lift the Dow Jones Transportation Average up 13 to about 2071.
New York Bagel rose to 10-3/4 from its IPO pricing of $9 a share in its Wall Street debut.
